# Phase 2 cleaning scorecard v3 (synthetic data)

*Generated by `src/score_cleaning.py` on 15 October 2026. Do not edit by hand. Earlier versions are frozen: v1 (`docs/phase2_scorecard_v1_holdout1.md`, before any held-out fix) and v2 (`docs/phase2_scorecard_v2_holdout2.md`, which holds the held-out-2 headline).*

**Fixed** = the cleaned value equals the true value. **Flagged** = the pipeline marked the cell or row for review. **Missed** = neither. Problems that cannot be detected from the files are excluded.

## Reading the held-out rounds

| Round | What it tests | Genuine errors fixed or flagged |
|---|---|---|
| Held-out 2 (first score, frozen v2) | Kinds of mess the cleaner had **never seen** | **92.9%** |
| Final round (Phase 7, frozen `docs/phase7_final_holdout_scorecard.md`) | The **same kinds of mess as held-out 2**, on **fresh data**, after the cleaner had been fixed against them | **98.1%** |

- **Held-out 2 measures robustness to new kinds of mess**: the figure to expect when real files bring problems nobody has seen.
- **The final round shows that the fixes generalise to new records**, not to new kinds of mess.
- Report both; never quote the final round alone.

## Why held-out 2 scored lower: officer FO06

FO06's sheets were only **partly** recognisable. The activity sheet had five known column names (District, Sector, Cell, Village, Total), so in v2 it was read, but its activity date, activity, project, status, female/male and cost columns had names the pipeline did not know (`Event date`, `Type of activity`, `Implementation status`, `Females`...). Those rows arrived without their key values: 364 were quarantined and many injected problems could not be seen. FO06's register was read without its registration number and registration date. That one officer's files pulled genuine errors from 96.1% to 92.9% and habits from 100% to 87.5%.

This round's fix 1 stops partial reads: a sheet missing any required field is now **skipped** with a message naming the missing fields and the unrecognised headers. The two right-hand columns show what that fix achieves alone, and then with the FO06 column names added to the config (`config/mapping_overlays/holdout2_fo06.yaml`, the lines a maintainer would paste into `source_mappings.yaml`). Neither replaces the headline.

## Known limitations

- 19 problems in the main set cannot be detected from the files (accepted 14 October 2026):

| error_type | detail | count |
|---|---|---|
| status_completed_but_late | this file has no planned date, so lateness cannot be seen | 13 |
| transcription_error | name spelling (cannot be detected without the paper form) | 6 |

- Nicknames (e.g. `Jado` for Jean de Dieu) are not recognised; there is deliberately no nickname list.
- Similar names, and initials matching a full name, are never merged without a phone or ID; they go to the review queue, so some true duplicates stay as two people until a person confirms them.
- Month-first dates (`Mar 12, 2024`) are not read, on purpose, until the partner says whether staff use them.
- An ID stored as a number in Excel has lost its 16th digit; it is flagged, but cannot be recovered.
- A sheet with unknown column names, or missing a required field, is skipped and reported, never read partly: its records are missing until a maintainer adds the column names to `config/source_mappings.yaml`.
- The synthetic data and the cleaner were written by the same team; real partner files are the real test.

#### (d) Duplicate beneficiaries: matching threshold

Pairs of registrations of the same person. Precision = share of matched pairs that are right; recall = share of true pairs found. Same national ID = always matched; otherwise names must score at least the threshold, in the same district and of the same sex, and are kept apart if phones differ by more than 1 digit, IDs differ, or ages differ by more than 2 years. The two lower variants switch rules off only to show what each rule contributes.

### Review queue and quarantine: Main set (seed 2023)

Each flag has one of three levels (`flag_severity` in config/settings.yaml): **critical** = row quarantined until the source file is corrected; **warning** = row used, but goes to the MEAL officer's review queue; **info** = counted as a data-quality measure, no one acts on a row. A row with any critical flag is quarantined and not also counted in the review queue.

Flags by level: critical 260, warning 376, info 1,563.

### Review queue and quarantine: Held-out 2 after this round's fixes (seen data)

Each flag has one of three levels (`flag_severity` in config/settings.yaml): **critical** = row quarantined until the source file is corrected; **warning** = row used, but goes to the MEAL officer's review queue; **info** = counted as a data-quality measure, no one acts on a row. A row with any critical flag is quarantined and not also counted in the review queue.

Flags by level: critical 486, warning 429, info 1,282.

#### (d) Duplicate beneficiaries: matching threshold

Pairs of registrations of the same person. Precision = share of matched pairs that are right; recall = share of true pairs found. Same national ID = always matched; otherwise names must score at least the threshold, in the same district and of the same sex, and are kept apart if phones differ by more than 1 digit, IDs differ, or ages differ by more than 2 years. The two lower variants switch rules off only to show what each rule contributes.

### Review queue and quarantine: Held-out 2 after the fixes + FO06 mapping in config (seen data)

Each flag has one of three levels (`flag_severity` in config/settings.yaml): **critical** = row quarantined until the source file is corrected; **warning** = row used, but goes to the MEAL officer's review queue; **info** = counted as a data-quality measure, no one acts on a row. A row with any critical flag is quarantined and not also counted in the review queue.

Flags by level: critical 1,588, warning 471, info 1,287.

#### Review queue (warnings) per month

At 2 minutes a row (an assumption to check with the MEAL officer), the budget of 60 minutes a month allows 30 rows.

- Rows to review over 36 months: **343**; per month: average **9.5**, median 10, busiest month 16 (2025-03), about 19 minutes a month on average.
- Months over the one-hour budget: **0**.

## Reconciliation scoring (main set)

The WASH-01 and AGR-01 reports are worked out from the same true data as the activity and register files, with discrepancies planted at known rates (decision log D132): two officers over-report 15 to 30% of the time, some months are under-reported by 20 to 50%, and a few figures have 1 to 5% rounding differences that should stay within the tolerance.

Scored at each indicator's comparison level (catalogue `derived.reconcile`, D162): WASH-01 by month (total), AGR-01 by quarter (total), by project and district. A gap needs more than the % tolerance AND at least 5 apart.

- Comparisons scored: 140; with a planted discrepancy: **47**; flagged: **22 (46.8%)**.
- Of these, **20** have a planted difference of at least 5; flagged: **19 (95.0%)**.

**Every flag raised (27), by what it caught:**

| What the flag caught | Flags |
|---|---|
| Planted discrepancies (over- or under-reporting) caught | 22 |
| Genuine data errors caught (an injected problem in the report or the records, e.g. an extra zero, quarantined or duplicate records) | 5 |
| Unexplained false alarms | 0 |

- Comparisons with only a planted rounding difference that stayed within the tolerance: 4 of 5.

| indicator_code | kind | outcome | comparisons |
|---|---|---|---|
| AGR-01 | none | correctly within tolerance | 16 |
| AGR-01 | planted | caught | 3 |
| AGR-01 | planted | missed (smaller than the minimum) | 17 |
| WASH-01 | none | correctly within tolerance | 68 |
| WASH-01 | none | flag explained: records-side data issue | 4 |
| WASH-01 | planted | caught | 19 |
| WASH-01 | planted | missed | 1 |
| WASH-01 | planted | missed (smaller than the minimum) | 7 |
| WASH-01 | rounding | correctly within tolerance | 4 |
| WASH-01 | rounding | flag explained: records-side data issue | 1 |

### Known limitation: planted discrepancies too small to detect

Of 66 planted report rows (the grain the officer reports: project, district, month and, for AGR-01, sex), **46** differ from the truth by less than 5 on their own (AGR-01: 39, WASH-01: 7). ## KoboToolbox exports (import adapter)

A test set where two sources come from KoboToolbox instead of Excel (`src/generate_kobo_exports.py`, D190): FO01's activities as an export with **XML values and headers**, and the WASH indicator reports as an export with **labels**. They are made from the main set's true records, with what a Kobo form cannot prevent injected: the same form submitted twice, and the optional cost left blank. Read with the production configuration (no overlay).

Sheets skipped: 0. Crash: no.

| Export | Rows | Repeated submissions removed | Cells compared | Cells correct | Optional costs left blank, kept blank | Quarantined | To review (why) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SYNTHETIC_ARDE_activity_monitoring_-_all_versions_-_xml_values_-_2026-06-30-17-00-00.xlsx | 780 | 21 of 21 | 9,108 | 9,108 (100.0%) | 41 of 41 | 0 | 0 (-) |
| SYNTHETIC_ARDE_indicator_report_WASH_-_all_versions_-_labels_-_2026-06-30-17-00-00.xlsx | 230 | 0 of 0 | 1,610 | 1,610 (100.0%) | 0 of 0 | 0 | 4 (accuracy_outlier) |

Rows to review in the Kobo exports are real data points (late entries and results above three times the target are in the true data), not reading errors.

## Changes made after seeing results

Every answer-key correction or scoring change made after results were seen, one line each. Details and evidence are in `docs/decision_log.md`. The frozen scorecards v1 and v2 were not rescored.

| Decision | What changed | Change |
|---|---|---|
| D54 | Answer key | 14 'completed but late' problems in the paper file relabelled undetectable (the paper form has no planned date); with 5 misspelt names, 19 problems left out of the genuine-error denominator. |
| D78 / D90 | Scorer | An age worked out from a date of birth is compared with the age from the TRUE date of birth and the true date of that registration (the key copied the first registration's age with +/-1). |
| D83 / D91 | Scorer | A blank age is a knock-on, not a miss, when the registration date on the same row carries an injected problem (all 7 cases checked by hand). |
| D136 | Scorer | A USD amount is judged against the amount the officer wrote, converted at the configured rate (the generator had rounded the USD figure before writing it). |
| D153 | Scoring rule | Reconciliation catch rate also reported for planted discrepancies at least the minimum difference (5) apart, after the minimum cut the raw catch rate to 30.3%; the raw figure is still reported. |
| D162 | Comparison level | Reconciliation compared at a level set per indicator (WASH-01 by month, AGR-01 by quarter, totals only), after AGR-01's monthly district figures proved mostly under the minimum. |
